intro: Books that have shaped how I think, and what I'm reading now. Pull one off the shelf.

books.title: The Qur'an
books.note: No other word can bring peace to its reader like the word of God.

books.title: The Sealed Nectar
books.author: Safiur Rahman Mubarakpuri
books.note: The seerah only multiplied my love for the Prophet (PBUH).

books.title: Philosophy in the Islamic World
books.author: Peter Adamson
books.note: An amazing intro to Islamic philosophy if you're ever interested!

books.title: How the World Thinks
books.author: Julian Baggini
books.note: This really broadened my horizons on how different peoples think and how close-minded we can be.

books.title: The Wretched of the Earth
books.author: Frantz Fanon
books.note: Violence is not just a necessity but an inevitability.

books.title: Orientalism
books.author: Edward W. Said
books.note: So many ideas built into us are derived from old, racist systems.

books.title: Rise and Kill First
books.author: Ronen Bergman
books.note: Truly eye-opening; brings a lot of context to the ongoing genocide of the Palestinian people.

books.title: The Lord of the Rings
books.author: J. R. R. Tolkien
books.note: I read this all in a week as a kid; I wish I had that kind of stamina now.

books.title: Hard to Be a God
books.author: Arkady and Boris Strugatsky
books.note: An absolute page-turner. The blend of philosophy and sci-fi kept me glued to the book and yearning for more.

books.title: Six Easy Pieces
books.author: Richard P. Feynman
books.note: Inspired my curiosity for learning and the wider world.

books.title: Welsh in 12 Weeks
books.author: Phylip and Julie Brake
books.note: Just an amazing textbook for Welsh learners, whether you're starting from zero or refreshing after school.
